release_notes: `app.py`: `square_off()`'s partial-close branch reported `total_pnl_pts: null` whenever a real close order landed unconfirmed — `_recompute_pnl()` only sets `total_pnl` once status is fully `CLOSED` (a contract `manual_exit()` relies on), and `square_off` had no separate running-total field the way `manual_exit`'s `pnl_pts_so_far` does. Now falls back to `_pnl_pts` (2026-09-01: DIB_07_Jul_2026_v2_Breeze's SqOff click toasted "+null pts"). `app.py`: real-mode close-order exceptions in `square_off()` were never logged anywhere durable — only into the transient HTTP response — leaving no way to diagnose a failure after the fact. Now logged via `logging.exception`. `broker/breeze_adapter.py`: exposed `find_recent_order(symbol, transaction_type, quantity)` — a public wrapper around the existing internal `_find_recent_order()` leg-identity match — so `strategies.engine.find_order_by_tag()`'s recovery path (used by `square_off`/`close_long_legs`/adjustment rolls when `place_order()` raises) works for Breeze too. Breeze has no order-tag/`orders()` equivalent to Kite/Dhan, so this was previously a guaranteed no-op for every Breeze strategy — any transient `place_order()` failure during a manual close was unrecoverable by the app (2026-09-01 incident, same strategy as above: LC/LP close orders raised with no way to confirm whether they'd actually reached ICICI). `find_order_by_tag()` and its 5 call sites (4 in `engine.py`, 1 in `app.py`) now thread `symbol`/`transaction_type`/`quantity` through for this fallback.
